Painter Blaster – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $80,000 – $110,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Painter Blasters to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Painter Blaster, you will be responsible for preparing, blasting, coating, and painting steel structures, mining equipment, industrial machinery, and fabricated components. You will ensure all surface preparation and protective coating work is completed safely, efficiently, and in accordance with project specifications, Australian Standards, and client requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret work instructions, technical drawings, and coating specifications.
•	Prepare steel surfaces by abrasive blasting, power tool cleaning, and other approved surface preparation methods.
•	Apply protective coatings, primers, sealers, and industrial paint systems using airless spray, conventional spray, brush, and roller techniques.
•	Mix paints and coatings in accordance with manufacturer specifications and project requirements.
•	Inspect prepared surfaces and completed coatings to ensure compliance with quality standards and required film thickness.
•	Perform touch-up work, maintenance painting, and coating repairs on mining and industrial equipment.
•	Safely operate blasting equipment, spray-painting equipment, compressors, and other associated tools.
•	Conduct routine maintenance and cleaning of painting and blasting equipment.
•	Maintain accurate records of completed work, coating materials used, and quality inspections.
•	Work collaboratively with supervisors, engineers, and other trades to meet project deadlines.
•	Assist with shutdown, maintenance, fabrication, and construction projects as required.
•	Follow all workplace health and safety policies, procedures, and environmental requirements.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Painter Blaster or in a similar industrial coatings role.
•	Experience in abrasive blasting, surface preparation, and industrial protective coatings.
•	Knowledge of industrial paint systems, coating application techniques, and quality inspection procedures.
•	Ability to read and interpret technical drawings and coating specifications.
•	Experience working in mining, oil and gas, construction, or heavy industrial environments is highly regarded.
•	Strong commitment to workplace safety, quality workmanship, and environmental compliance.
•	Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
•	Excellent communication and organisational skills.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $80,000 – $110,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.

result.description:
UE Tech builds software for the local government sector. We develop and maintain two main products: Monitor CRMS, an engagement platform used by councils, and DevCAP, an infrastructure / development contributions (ICP/DCP) administration package — alongside supporting applications and internal tools. We are a small, hands-on development team based in Brunswick.

The role
We are hiring a mid-level developer to work across our product portfolio. Monitor CRMS is currently being re-engineered from a legacy .NET Framework codebase to .NET 10, and you will contribute to both maintaining the existing applications and building out the new platform. This is a full-stack role on a small team — you will work across the back end, database, and front end with limited supervision, and have direct contact with customers to shape what gets built.

What you'll do
Build, maintain, and extend C#/.NET applications (current target framework .NET 10)
Work with SQL Server — writing and optimising queries, schema work, troubleshooting data issues
Develop front-end features in React / Node.js
Deploy and support applications running on Azure
Design and implement complex business-rules logic, configurable workflows, and approval / administration processes
Work directly with customers to understand their needs, clarify requirements, and translate them into technical solutions
Diagnose and fix bugs across existing line-of-business applications
Use AI-assisted development tools as a standard part of the workflow (this is core to how we work)

What we're looking for
1-2 years' commercial software development experience
Solid C# / .NET skills, including maintaining and modernising existing codebases
Working SQL Server experience (querying, schema, performance)
Front-end experience with React and Node.js
Familiarity with Azure-hosted applications
Demonstrated experience building complex line-of-business applications — business-rules-heavy systems, configurable workflows, approvals, or regulatory / statutory process logic
Strong communication skills, with the ability to engage non-technical stakeholders, draw out requirements, and explain technical concepts clearly
Ability to work autonomously across the full stack on a small team
Comfortable adopting AI-assisted development tools day to day
A degree in computer science / software engineering, or equivalent commercial experience

Desirable
Experience modernising legacy .NET Framework applications to current .NET
Experience with CRM, planning, local-government, or public-sector software
Familiarity with development contributions, planning schemes, or similar regulatory domains

Location: In office Brunswick, this is not a remote role.
Work Rights: Applicants must have valid Australian work rights
To apply: Attach your resume and a short cover letter, outlining why you would be a good fit for this role.

Position Overview:
Ebcon is an Australian-owned construction, civil works and maintenance company delivering infrastructure, road maintenance, restoration, and electrical works projects for councils, government agencies and commercial clients. The company is recognised for its commitment to quality workmanship, safety, compliance and reliable project delivery.

As an Estimator at Ebcon, you will be responsible for preparing accurate cost estimates and tender submissions for a diverse range of civil construction and infrastructure projects. This position requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail and the ability to work collaboratively with project teams.

Responsibilities and Tasks:

•	Evaluate and interpret civil engineering, infrastructure and construction drawings, specifications and contract documentation to prepare accurate cost estimates for infrastructure, road maintenance, restoration and electrical works projects.
•	Conduct quantity take-offs and prepare detailed cost estimates using industry-standard estimating software.
•	Prepare detailed cost estimates, tender submissions, feasibility assessments and pricing proposals for civil construction, maintenance and infrastructure projects.
•	Liaise with subcontractors, suppliers and service providers to obtain competitive quotations for labour, materials, plant and specialised services.
•	Analyse project risks, cost variations and scope changes, preparing updated estimates and forecasts throughout the tender and project lifecycle.
•	Review project specifications, site conditions and client requirements to identify cost-saving opportunities while maintaining quality, safety and compliance standards.
•	Collaborate with project managers, engineers and operational teams to develop practical estimating solutions that support successful delivery of infrastructure and maintenance projects.
•	Maintain accurate estimating records, cost databases and tender documentation, ensuring submissions comply with council, government agency and commercial client requirements.

Qualifications and Skills:

•	Relevant qualification.
•	Minimum 1 year experience as an Estimator.
•	Strong understanding of civil construction methodologies, materials and cost structures.
•	Proficiency with estimating software and Microsoft Office Suite.
•	Excellent analytical, numerical and communication skills.
•	Ability to manage multiple tenders and deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Salary:
The role offers a remuneration package ranging from $79,000 – $95,000 p.a. plus superannuation for a 38-hour work week.

result.description:
Blood Borne Virus / Sexually Transmitted Infections RN 

 Role Overview 

 Provide sexual and blood-borne virus (BBV) testing, treatment, education and prevention services in clinical and community settings. 

 Key Responsibilities 

  Clinical Care  

 
	 
	 Assess clients and provide testing for BBVs (HIV, hepatitis B & C) and STIs. 
	 
	 
	 Collect specimens (blood, swabs) and manage results and follow-up. 
	 
	 
	 Provide treatment, health advice, counselling and referrals within scope of practice. 
	 
	 
	 Support prevention activities such as vaccinations and harm-reduction education. 
	 
 

  Community & Public Health  

 
	 
	 Deliver health education on safer sex, transmission, testing and prevention. 
	 
	 
	 Work with doctors, allied health and community workers. 
	 
	 
	 Assist with contact tracing and public health follow-up. 
	 
 

  Administration & Quality  

 
	 
	 Maintain accurate clinical records and reports. 
	 
	 
	 Contribute to service improvement, audits, education and training. 
	 
 

 Skills & Qualifications 

 
	 
	 Registered Nurse (AHPRA) – essential. 
	 
	 
	 Experience in sexual health, community or public health nursing preferred. 
	 
	 
	 Strong skills in assessment, specimen collection, counselling and education. 
	 
	 
	 Excellent communication, cultural sensitivity and non-judgmental approach. 
	 
	 
	 Postgraduate training in sexual/reproductive health or public health is desirable. 
	 
 

 Work Settings 

 
	 
	 Sexual health clinics 
	 
	 
	 Community and outreach programs 
	 
	 
	 Public health and prevention services 
	 
   Apply Now

result.description:
The Company

Ararat Family Restaurant is a 24-hour full-service restaurant that offers well-priced hearty breakfasts, lunch, and la carte dinners with a seating capacity of more than 120 patrons. We are committed to providing the best culinary experience and maintaining the highest hygiene standards. This is a rare opportunity to work in a rewarding environment as part of a creative kitchen brigade.

About the Role

The restaurant provides breakfast, lunch, dinner and a function menu filled with colourful, nutritious, and organic fare 7 days a week.  The Chef position intends to lead the restaurant kitchen in cooking food, creating, and cooking meals unique to the restaurant. The primary objective of the role is to prepare uniform dishes and be responsible for maintaining a safe and healthy work environment. We are currently seeking a Chef (for a full-time position) which is critical to our ability to operate the business.

Job Description

Position: Chef
Location of work: 8475 Western Hwy, Ararat VIC 3377
Employment type: Permanent, Full time
Salary Range: $75,000 - $85,000 plus Guranteed Superannuation

The main duties of the position include: 
     
•	Coordinate & participate in the cooking and preparation of all the food items present in the restaurant’s menu.
•	Assist with planning tasks and building food menus in the restaurant.
•	Planning menus, overseeing the kitchen staff, and ensuring that the food meets high-quality standards.
•	Ensure that each dish is nutritious, and cost-effective and collaborate with a team of kitchen staff to deliver food that meets the highest quality standards.
•	Taking stock of ingredients and equipment and placing orders to replenish stock.
•	Coordinating kitchen staff and assisting them as required.
•	Training staff to prepare and cook all the menu items.
•	Setting up the kitchen with cooking utensils and equipment like knives, pans, and food scales.
•	Slightly modify recipes to meet customer’s needs and requests.
•	Ensure compliance with all health and safety regulations within the kitchen area.
•	Ensuring impeccable presentation and garnishing.
•	Make sure that other kitchen staff that work under him adhere to standards of cooking.
•	Able to initiate new ideas in cooking methods to bring up fresh and attractive ideas that will generate more sales.
•	Strictly adhere to the budget of the restaurant by ensuring that supplies are in line with the budget and supervising food and labour costs.
•	Monitor and maintain stock levels to place orders for supplies when due.
•	Monitor and oversee sanitation practices to ensure that regulations and standards of cleanliness are always being strictly adhered to by employees.
•	Managing relationships with distributors and resolving any issues with vendors, promptly.
•	Follow proper handling and the right temperature of all food products.
•	Helps the executive chef research and test new food products in conjunction with maintaining all standard recipes.
•	Trains associate with safety procedures and supervise their ability to follow loss prevention policies to prevent accidents and control costs.
•	Balances nutritional value of menus and ensures the quality of the total service program.
•	Interact with the guests to receive their feedback on food quality, service levels and presentation.
•	Aware of control of substances hazardous to health and chemical safety.
•	Review staffing levels to ensure that guest service, operational needs and financial objectives are met.
•	 Ensuring that the food items are stocked properly in refrigerators and freezers.
•	Conduct menu abstract analysis and engineering functions to improve profit and quality.
•	Evaluate changes in guest needs, the guest mix, industry, and competitive trends.
•	Make sure adequate numbers of kitchen staff are scheduled to handle each banquet properly.
•	Possesses the ability to handle any menu ranging from breakfast buffets to corporate lunch meetings with sandwiches to formal dinners that are individually plated.
•	Be able to express creativity through food selections, preparation, and presentation.
•	Maintain healthy relationships with customers and colleagues.
•	Supervising kitchen staff demonstrating techniques and advising on cooking procedures.
•	Communicating any food preparation issues with management, Dietitians, kitchen and wait staff.  

Qualifications required:
•	At least Diploma in Hospitality Management or relevant work experience to substitute the qualification requirement. 
•	A minimum of 1 year of relevant work experience is required.

Key attributes/ Skills:
•	Communication
•	Leadership
•	Interpersonal skills. 
•	Capable of delegating multiple tasks.
•	Excellent record of kitchen management. 
•	Excellent time management skills. 
•	Perfection in sanitation and quality control. 
•	Knowledge of all safety standards.  

 Interested in the role? Apply for the role if you think you meet the criteria, and we’ll get in contact with you shortly. Only eligible candidates will be contacted.
result.title: Chef

Dunsteel Engineering Pty Ltd is a leading steel fabrication business with over 50 years of experience. We specialise in delivering complex projects for leading building firms and architects. Complete work involving structural steel
Complete tasks involving welding out

Join metal sections and structures together using welding, bolting or riveting methods
Perform assigned duties in a timely and safe manner

Assist in the management of a harmonious environment, team building and training of apprentices and other employees as required.
Adherence to company procedures.

Excellent attention to detail

result.description:
Advanced Scaffolder / Scaffolder – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $80,000 – $110,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking experienced and motivated Advanced Scaffolders / Scaffolders to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As an Advanced Scaffolder / Scaffolder, you will be responsible for erecting, altering, dismantling, and maintaining scaffolding structures to support construction, maintenance, shutdown, and industrial projects. You will work closely with supervisors and project teams to ensure all scaffolding is installed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with Australian Standards and workplace safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Read and interpret scaffolding plans, drawings, and specifications.
•	Erect, alter, inspect, and dismantle scaffolding systems for commercial, industrial, and mining projects.
•	Ensure scaffolding structures are safe, secure, and compliant with Australian Standards and site requirements.
•	Install edge protection, temporary access platforms, stair systems, handrails, and safety barriers.
•	Conduct routine inspections of scaffolding and identify defects or maintenance requirements.
•	Load, unload, transport, and organise scaffolding materials and equipment.
•	Safely use hand tools, power tools, lifting equipment, and access equipment.
•	Work effectively at heights while following all safety procedures and risk management requirements.
•	Collaborate with supervisors, engineers, and other trades to ensure project deadlines are achieved.
•	Maintain accurate records of inspections, maintenance, and completed work where required.
•	Assist in mentoring apprentices and junior scaffolders.
•	Comply with all workplace health and safety policies, procedures, and site regulations.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1–2 years of full-time experience as a Scaffolder or Advanced Scaffolder.
•	Ability to read and interpret scaffolding drawings and technical specifications.
•	Experience erecting and dismantling various scaffolding systems in industrial, mining, or construction environments.
•	Strong understanding of safe work practices, working at heights, and Australian scaffolding standards.
•	Ability to work safely in physically demanding environments and at heights.
•	Strong problem-solving, communication, and teamwork skills.
•	High attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
•	Relevant High Risk Work Licence (Scaffolding) and Working at Heights certification will be highly regarded.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $80,000 – $110,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing training and career development.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.
